title: Targeted inference tweak notes for conversational SLA
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a focused, spreadsheet-driven memo with targeted recommendations for conversational workloads (short-turn chat, 2–8 exchanges, average request tokens 20–60) where teams demand a P50 latency <= 60ms and a 99th percentile <= 250ms at scale. The goal: a reproducible set of tuning defaults (batching, cache policies, q-config suggestions) and a short mapping from the cost-model spreadsheet outputs to an operational action plan.

Why this is different:
Most existing presets are broad (general mixed workloads). This note translates cost-sweeper outputs into a small set of recommended knobs for chat-first customers, with explicit guardrails and spreadsheet lines referenced by label so engineers can re-run sensitivity sweeps and confirm cost delta.

Spreadsheet model references (local sheet tabs):
- tab: convo_profile_baseline — baseline traces and token histograms used as input to cost sweeper
- tab: cost_sweep_2048seq — cost and latency for varying batch sizes at different qconfigs and model variants
- tab: cache_sim_convo — TTL, hit-rate simulation, traffic cohort splits
- tab: autoscale_headroom — simulated instances/GPUs per 1k rps under different burst profiles

Key assumptions used in numbers below (verifiable in spreadsheet):
- Average prompt + response per request: 40 tokens (20 inbound, 20 outbound)
- Typical model: opensim-xxl-16g variant (quantized variants available)
- Baseline target SLO: P50 <= 60ms; P99 <= 250ms
- Acceptable quality delta threshold for quantization: max 1.5 point drop on proprietary BLEU-like eval or <3% top-level metric degradation on conversational turn adequacy judged by eval set

High-level recommendations (actionable):
1) Batching defaults (conversational profile)
   - Target dynamic batch size: 8–16 for low-latency pools. Rationale: sweeper shows batch 8 reduces cost by ~14% vs batch 1 with P50 within target; batch 16 pushes P99 close to limit in peaky bursts.
   - Max allowed batch window: 12ms. Use continuous batching with a short batching window (max-latency cap) to avoid tail amplification.
   - Prefer request-aware batching: allow small-request early flush for requests that have long-tail histories (long prompt prefixes).

2) KV / prefix caching
   - Prefix cache TTLs: cohort-based TTLs recommended. Set session-heavy users (heavy repeat prefixes) TTL=3600s; ephemeral users TTL=120s.
   - Aim for effective prefix-hit rate >= 38% for session cohort to see 10–18% cost improvement (sheet cache_sim_convo shows breakpoints at 20%, 35%, 50%).
   - Cache population strategy: eager store on first generation for repeatable templates; sample 10% of unique prefixes for telemetry to avoid cache pollution.

3) Quantization policy (qconfig) and fallback rules
   - Default for new customers: aggressively test 4-bit quant (awq/ptq 4-bit per-channel) on a canary pool (5% traffic) for models <= 16G. If eval metrics drop <1% on our conversational eval set, expand to 25% traffic and monitor user-facing regressions for 48 hours.
   - Fallback to 8-bit when: P99 latency decreases but quality regressions exceed threshold OR model exhibits hallucination increases in RL-filtered tests.
   - For critical accounts that require deterministic quality, restrict to INT8/float16 only and use quantized models behind dedicated capacity rather than shared hosts.

4) Autoscale and headroom settings for conversational pools
   - Target steady-state headroom: 18–25% free capacity per GPU to absorb 95th percentile bursts without immediate scale-up. This reduces throttle/queue spikes that push P99 above 250ms. See autoscale_headroom tab for simulated cost tradeoffs.
   - Minimum burst placement: allow single-increment fast-burst spin-up with pre-warmed micro-instances (cold-start latency <300ms).

5) Routing and model-variant fallbacks
   - Route by cost vs latency policy: prefer quantized variant for non-enterprise traffic; for enterprise customers with SLA flag, prefer float16 variant.
   - Automatic fallback chain: quantized -> int8 -> float16. If latency spikes or error rate increases 2x baseline, temporarily route 10% of requests to the next tier up and observe.

6) Logging/telemetry hooks to drive continuous cost tuning
   - Add telemetry labels to requests: cohort, prefix-hash, observed-cache-hit, batch-size, qconfig, model-variant.
   - Daily aggregation: compute per-cohort P50/P95/P99, cost-per-1k-requests, cache-hit, and quality-sample rate. Feed top-100 offending prefixes into a short list to evaluate caching or template-normalization.

Concrete example configurations (starting point)
- Small chat pool (low latency): dynamic_batch_size=8, max_batch_window_ms=12, qconfig=4bit-canary, prefix_cache_TTL_sec=120 (ephemeral cohort), autoscale_headroom=20%
- Medium chat pool (balanced): dynamic_batch_size=12, max_batch_window_ms=15, qconfig=8bit-default, prefix_cache_TTL_sec=600 (session cohort), autoscale_headroom=22%
- Enterprise-reliable pool: dynamic_batch_size=6, max_batch_window_ms=10, qconfig=float16, prefix_cache_TTL_sec=3600 (session cohort), autoscale_headroom=30%

Interpreting the spreadsheet outputs (how to run a follow-up tweak)
1) Run cost_sweep_2048seq with your actual request-length histogram (tab: convo_profile_baseline). 2) Pick target P50/P99 constraints and filter rows with meeting latency constraints. 3) From those rows, pick qconfig that minimizes cost but keep quality within threshold. 4) Simulate cache hit-rate in cache_sim_convo with candidate TTLs. 5) Recompute autoscale impacts using autoscale_headroom tab.

Risks and guardrails
- Over-caching: high TTLs with low cardinality prefixes may lock stale behavior; include cache eviction metric and TTL decay schedules.
- Quantization regressions: some prompt types (programming, numeric) degrade more under 4-bit; include focused eval slices and do canary releases for those customers.
- Batching tail risk: large batches reduce cost but can increase P99 during peaky traffic; enforce batch-window caps and enforce burst routing to dedicated low-latency lanes if we observe repeated P99 violations.

Open items and next steps (owners assigned)
- Run an isolated 2-week canary of 4-bit on a non-critical region and return a regression report (owner: Marcus Chen, due: 2025-02-14).
- Add prefix-hash and cache telemetry labels to RPC schema (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2025-02-07).
- Create a small synthetic traffic generator for burst scenarios used by autoscale_headroom tab (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2025-02-11).

Appendix: quick diff from the baseline (example numbers from cost_sweep_2048seq):
- Batch 1 -> Batch 8: cost delta -14%, P50 change +6ms, P99 change +18ms (still within target for balanced pools).
- Adding prefix cache (hit 40%): incremental cost -11% on top of batching.
- Quant 4-bit (canary pass): cost -22% additional vs float16; small degradation on answer adequacy (~0.8 points) on convo eval.

If you want, I can: 1) export the exact rows from the spreadsheet for the three concrete configs above; 2) produce a short evaluation checklist for the 4-bit canary tests; or 3) convert the recommendations into a YAML config draft to be consumed by the orchestration team.

Status: in_review — asking product + serving runtime for quick engineering feasibility and SRE for autoscale safety signoff before rolling to canary.
